description: A second `struct` declaring an already-declared type name raises `ol-duplicate-definition` at phase-1 registration, carrying BOTH spans: `source_span` at the later declaration (line 2) and `params.original_span` at the earlier one (line 1), so the message can name the line the learner already used (`spec/error-model.md:126,144-147`). Ruling #833 rule 6 gives redefining YOUR OWN name its own code, leaving `ol-reserved-word` with exactly one meaning. The field lists deliberately DIFFER (`[ x y ]` vs `[ a b ]`) so this fixture cannot pass under a rule that only notices two identical declarations. `check()` reports the identical code, params and spans for this program. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
